A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, detection framework, and retained experiments. All 14 pages of v2 and 24 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison; no material reading gaps were found.

before.justification: v2 reports original detection experiments on open-source models and public APIs, sampling and diversity analyses, multi-key experiments, and watermark-parameter estimates.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds power simulations, further model evaluations, adversarial experiments, SynthID-Text detection, and an entropy-conditioned watermark study.

M1.justification: The three core detection tests remain substantially unchanged, but v3 extends the methodological scope with an entropy-conditioned AAR generation algorithm that gates watermarking on preceding-token information content (Appendix F.6, Algorithm 6). Its SynthID adaptation also requires H = h and recommends context estimation as preprocessing. Algorithms 1–5 primarily document existing procedures.

E1.justification: v3 adds detection scenarios involving no-cache watermarks, SynthID-Text, query-level and token-level watermark disabling, and entropy-conditioned AAR (Appendices F.3–F.6). It also introduces C4-prompted generation for evaluating watermark strength. These substantially extend the tested conditions and task coverage beyond v2.

E2.justification: Neither version benchmarks the proposed presence tests against an external black-box presence-detection method. The added watermark schemes are detection targets. The private-key AAR detector in Figure 6 measures watermark strength in generated text, rather than serving as a competing method for the same presence-detection task.

E3.justification: The main query budgets are retained, but v3 adds YI1.5-9B and QWEN2-7B configurations, GEMMA-7B SynthID evaluation, controlled power simulations, and rejection-rate metrics at 1% and 5%. The entropy-conditioned study introduces 100 C4-prompted completions of 200 tokens, alongside the existing 1,000-query, 50-token presence test. These are substantial additions to evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2's sampling, diversity, multi-key, and parameter-estimation analyses are retained. v3 adds power-versus-query curves, context-estimation distributions, no-cache and SynthID case studies, query/token disabling tests, and an entropy-versus-watermark-strength investigation (Figures 4–6 and Appendices E–F). These materially broaden robustness and failure-boundary analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions already report 100 repetitions, five Red-Green keys, and bootstrap-based uncertainty. v3 clarifies random key selection, specifies 1,000 repetitions for the new power simulations, and adds rejection-frequency summaries with an explicit statement that multiple testing is unadjusted. This extends statistical reporting without establishing increased repetitions for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Some retained numerical results change: the LLAMA2-7B Fixed-Sampling p-value at key length 2048 changes from 1.0e-8 in v2 Table 3 to 0.003 in v3 Table 4 under the reported retained setup. Extensive new results include SynthID's reported median p-value of 0.000 and a detection failure at 5% token disabling with key length 2048 (p = 0.65, Table 9). Public-API Table 2 and key-length estimates remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds explicit within-regime logit-invariance and cross-boundary separation properties for context estimation (Appendix B.1, Equations 13–15), beyond v2's brief distribution-change argument. It also mathematically specifies the new entropy-gating rule. The central permutation-test, rarefaction, and multi-key derivations remain, with no new proof of detection power or undetectability.

C1.justification: v2's introduction and conclusion recommend deprioritizing undetectability and suggest that avoiding practical detection may be inherently difficult. v3 narrows the conclusion to detectability of popular practical schemes and presents improved stealth as a research direction. Parameter estimation, already present in v2 Appendix C, is promoted to a headline contribution alongside robustness to additional schemes and modifications.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 replaces v2's suggestion that tested APIs are unwatermarked with an inconclusive interpretation of non-rejection. v3 explicitly acknowledges the absence of theoretical power guarantees and discusses entropy-conditioned stealth versus watermark strength, unevaluated properties, and potentially stronger adversarial modifications. These materially qualify applicability and the interpretation of successful detection.

D1.justification: v3 supplies code-access information and describes its coverage of core tests, deployed-model tests, and appendix experiments; v2 provides no corresponding project-code disclosure. Algorithms 1–5 expand procedural documentation, Algorithm 6 specifies the new variant, and Appendix G adds query/token accounting and dated pricing assumptions. These are substantial reproducibility additions, although some documentation is internally inconsistent.

R1.justification: v3 substantially develops the relationship to theoretical undetectability through Christ et al. and practical constraints discussed through Fairoze et al. It also engages with Aaronson's AAR and SynthID-Text to motivate new investigations, and adds Zhang et al. on watermark stealing. This broadens research positioning beyond bibliographic updates to retained works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion are substantially revised. The appendices are reorganized: parameter estimation moves from C to B, scheme details from B to D, and extended experiments from A to F. Separate practical-implications, algorithm-description, power-analysis, cost-analysis, and ethics/reproducibility sections create a substantially different narrative structure.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 4–6, Tables 5–10, and six algorithm blocks, and expands the retained appendix results table. Figure 1 moves into the introduction, while the public-API table changes from a wrapped placement to a centered display. Conference formatting also changes typography and page layout throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the paper through more cautious conclusions, experiments exposing power and robustness limits, and substantial reproducibility documentation. However, new reporting defects limit these gains: for YI1.5-9B with LeftHash (2, 0.25), Tables 5–6 report rejection rates of 0.00 at 5% significance but 1.00 at 1%; Algorithm 3 also thresholds using estimated variance where Section 2 specifies standard deviation. The broader evidence is useful, but these inconsistencies weaken confidence in its reporting and reproduction.
